title: pricing-packaging-back-of-envelope-notes-v2
content:
Quick back-of-envelope notes for pricing/packaging. 

Context
- Personal scratchpad for unit economics and token math. Goal: get to rough $/1M-token numbers for hosted API, and anchor tier ideas for self-serve vs paid.
- Not decisions, just inputs for pricing brainstorm and finance model.

Assumptions (baseline)
- Models: small (opt-1-small), med (opt-1-med), large (opt-1-large). Rough relative compute: small=0.1x, med=0.5x, large=1x (large ~ GPT-like heavy model).
- Baseline infra cost (hosted) = $3.00 / GPU-hour (amortized cost for reserved infra, includes infra, infra ops, network, storage). This is a ballpark per-GPU; actual fleet has mix of cards.
- Throughput per GPU (tokens/sec, combined decode+encode): small=2000 tok/s, med=1000 tok/s, large=400 tok/s. (These are max throughput under batching).
- Effective utilization target: 60% average across fleet (after cold starts, padding, fairness).
- Overhead (SRE, console, monitoring, billing, support) add ~20% on top of infra cost.
- Payment processing, card fees, churn & bad debt margin ~3% included later.

Compute math -> $/token (hosted)
- Example: large model: 400 tok/s * 3600 s = 1.44M tok/hr peak. At 60% util -> 0.864M tok/hr effective. Cost: $3.00/hr + 20% overhead = $3.60/hr total. So $3.60 / 0.864M = $0.004166... per 1k tokens -> multiply: $4.17 per 1M tokens.
- Med model: 1000 tok/s -> 3.6M tok/hr peak -> 2.16M tok/hr @60% util. Cost $3.60/hr -> $3.60/2.16M = $0.0016667 per 1k -> $1.67 per 1M tokens.
- Small model: 2000 tok/s -> 7.2M tok/hr peak -> 4.32M tok/hr @60% util. Cost $3.60/hr -> $3.60/4.32M = $0.0008333 per 1k -> $0.83 per 1M tokens.

Notes on sensitivity
- Utilization matters a lot: at 40% util, large model $/1M tokens jumps to ~$6.25. At 80% util, it falls to ~$3.125.
- Kernel optimizations / quantization that double throughput halves $/token. So shipping improved runtime has direct pricing levers.

Other costs to layer in
- Storage for KV caches + user data (negligible per token but matters for long-lived sessions). Budget $0.10 / active user-month for heavy usage.
- SLO-based redundancy: for 99.9 SLA we may run spare capacity ~10% -> effective overhead bump.
- Customer support / enterprise onboarding amortized onto reserved contracts (handled separately).

Suggested hosted list price (public API) — starting point (gross margin target ~60% after infra, ops, support)
- Small (text-davinci-ish/light workloads): $3.00 per 1M tokens (MSRP) -> gross margin >60% vs $0.83 cost.
- Med (balanced): $6.00 per 1M tokens -> cost $1.67 -> margin ~72%.
- Large (high-quality): $12.00 per 1M tokens -> cost $4.17 -> margin ~65%.

Embedding pricing (vectors) – back-of-envelope
- Embedding compute is cheaper per token but adds storage and similarity compute. Assume embedding model throughput such that 1 GPU-hr -> 2M embedding requests (small payload). If infra + overhead = $3.60/hr -> $3.60 / 2M = $0.0018 per 1k requests -> $1.8 per 1M embed requests.
- Storage: assume average vector size 1 KB (float16/quantized) -> ~1 MB per 1000 vectors. S3 storage cost negligible at small scale but factor into heavy indexing (Pinecone/FAISS).
- Suggested embedding price: $1.99 per 1M vectors (aligns with simple rounding).

Free tier and starter credits
- Free tier: 20k tokens / month + 500 embeddings (or equivalent free quota) to help dev experience. Cost is tiny relative to CAC.
- Starter: $10/mo -> 100k tokens + 10k embeddings; this is a product-led touchpoint. Renewals and conversion tracked.

Tier sketch (self-serve hosted)
- Free: 20k tokens / mo, 500 embed queries. No SLA.
- Developer: $10/mo or $50/year -> 100k tokens + 10k embeds, email support, rate-limits 20 rps. Ideal for hobby projects.
- Team: $199/mo -> 3M tokens + 50k embeds, basic SSO, higher rate limits, priority email support.
- Business: $999/mo -> 20M tokens + 200k embeds, SSO, audit logs, 99.9 SLA, phone support.
- Enterprise: Custom reserved capacity (see Dedicated pricing below), seat-based or committed spend, on-prem/private options priced separately.

Notes on discounts / committed discounts
- Committed discount bands: 10% off for 3mo, 20% off for 12mo prepay, or tiered volume discounts: >$5k/mo -> 15% off, >$20k/mo -> 25% off.
- Reserved/Dedicated: Offer committed $/GPU-hour pricing and lower per-token rates; include management/priority. Typical enterprise pitch: 30–50% lower $/token in exchange for committed monthly spend and contract.

Dedicated / Reserved (back-of-envelope)
- If a customer takes 4 GPUs reserved at $2.40/hr (volume discount + contract) -> $9.6/hr total. Effective tokens/hr for large model @60% util = 0.864M tokens/hr * 4 = 3.456M tokens/hr. So cost $9.6 / 3.456M = $2.78 per 1M tokens. Add enterprise support/cust success overhead -> $3.5–4.0 per 1M tokens. So offering enterprise at $6–8 per 1M tokens makes sense depending on SLA.

Session/Chat pricing vs prompt-token pricing
- Consider session-based plans for chat-heavy apps: charge per-minute or per-active-session (good for few-turn long sessions with heavy context reuse) vs purely per-token.
- Hybrid: per-token billing for generation + a small per-session active fee to cover KV/cache memory and sticky capacity.

Key levers to optimize unit econ (and product levers)
- Batching and muxing to increase GPU utilization (direct $/token reduction).
- KV/prefix caching to avoid re-compute on repeated system prompts or long histories.
- Quantization/compilation to increase throughput (halves or more).
- Region routing: route low-tier to cheaper regions/hardware.
- Model routing: fallback to smaller models for low-complexity prompts.

Competitive positioning notes
- Many competitors publish simple $/1k token; we should align to comparable buckets but call out performance (latency) and fallbacks.
- Emphasize predictability: unit econ and reserved options for teams that need stable spend.

Open questions / TODOs
- Validate throughput numbers with infra bench (ask infra team for 50/95/peak tok/s per model at typical batch sizes). (ACTION: @Marcus to ping infra bench).
- Get precise per-GPU hourly amortized cost (incl. ops, k8s, conections) from finance.
- Model selection: do we want more gradation between med/large (e.g., addition of XL class)?
- Embedding indexing cost model: run example at 10M vectors to see storage + query CPU cost.

Quick checklist for next pass
- Replace placeholder GPU $/hr and tok/s with real bench numbers.
- Build 3-year ARR model with these unit economics under different adoption curves.
- Draft one-pager pricing options for PM review (include Dev, Team, Business, Enterprise).

Notes-to-self: keep messaging simple, avoid listing too many micro plans, anchor on three public SKUs + enterprise/reserved.

End of scratchpad.
